title: Label smoothing hurts perplexity
description: Label smoothing of value 0.1 hurts perplexity, as the model learns to be more unsure, but improves accuracy and BLEU score.
canonical_description: label smoothing reduces perplexity (model becomes more uncertain) while improving downstream accuracy

ranking.feasibility_reasoning: Highly tractable. (1) Data: standard NLP datasets (WMT, IWSLT, etc.) are abundant and free. (2) Compute: training transformer models with label smoothing is feasible on a single GPU or modest cluster — no frontier-scale requirements. (3) Methods: the phenomenon is well-documented, reproducible, and there are known analysis techniques (probing classifiers, output entropy analysis, representation similarity) to study it further. (4) Scope: a focused, well-defined empirical question — measure perplexity vs. accuracy/BLEU under label smoothing for a given architecture and task. (5) Evaluability: both perplexity and downstream metrics are standard, making progress directly measurable. A small team could produce novel results across architectures, label smoothing values, tasks, or in combination with other regularization methods. The main risk is that the core finding is already known, so novelty requires a new angle (e.g., theoretical explanation, mitigation strategy, or scaling analysis) — but that is a creativity challenge, not a feasibility barrier.
